newsitem.title: BELGIUM: WEU meets to discuss NATO links, new arms group.
newsitem.headline: WEU meets to discuss NATO links, new arms group.

text.p: Foreign and defence ministers of the Western European Union (WEU) defence grouping began meeting on Tuesday to discuss the WEU's growing links with NATO and to forge a new armaments research agreement.
The ministers were also expected to discuss what, if anything, the WEU could contribute to help the Canadian-led humanitarian effort in Africa's troubled Great Lakes region.

The WEU, often described as the European Union's fledgling defence arm, comprises 10 EU members -- all but Austria, Denmark, Sweden, Ireland and Finland, whose ministers were attending the Ostend meeting as observers.

Tuesday's meeting also was aimed at bringing together ministers from three non-EU NATO members, Norway, Turkey and Iceland, and 10 eastern European and Baltic states that have been offered eventual EU membership.
Top item on the ministers agenda was the new relationship agreed between the WEU and the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO).

With the blessing of NATO's leading force, the United States, the two groups have agreed to develop so-called Combined Joint Task Forces (CJTF) under which the WEU will be lent NATO equipment and troops for European-only projects.
Part of a growing desire from some countries to have a European identity within NATO, the plan is for the WEU to conduct humanitarian and peacekeeping missions without the United States and Canada.

The ministers were also expected to create a Western European Armaments Organisation to pool weapons research at a time of cutbacks in defence budgets. This group would include the WEU 10, plus Denmark, Norway and Turkey.
Officials said the group may eventually become involved in joint weapons procurement.
